title: Multi-Level Aggregation (Aggregate of Aggregates)
description: Find the **average number of orders placed per customer per month** across all customer-month combinations. You cannot use AVG(COUNT(*)) directly — use a two-level aggregation: first count orders per customer per month in a subquery, then average those counts in the outer query.
solution_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(monthly_count), 2) AS avg_orders_per_customer_month FROM (SELECT customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date) AS order_month, COUNT(*) AS monthly_count FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date)) sub

test_cases.description: 6 customer-month combos: C1(Jan=2,Feb=1), C2(Jan=2,Feb=2), C3(Jan=1,Mar=2). Average = 10/6 ≈ 1.67

hints: Use a subquery (or CTE) to first compute COUNT(*) per customer per month using GROUP BY customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', order_date).
Then wrap it in an outer SELECT and apply AVG() to the monthly_count column — you cannot nest aggregate functions like AVG(COUNT(*)) directly.
explanation: Direct AVG(COUNT(*)) is not allowed in standard SQL because you cannot nest aggregate functions. The solution uses a two-level aggregation: the inner query groups by customer and month to produce a monthly_count per row, then the outer query averages those counts. This pattern — aggregate of aggregates — always requires a subquery or CTE as an intermediate step.
